_comment: Curated source list — the starred sites, and what we are permitted to do with each.
This file is the source of truth, not sources.db. The database is gitignored and
rebuilt from data/, so a star stored only in SQLite would vanish on the next rebuild.
Starring in the admin writes back to this file; editing it in VS Code works too.
required  — always queried directly, not just when a search surfaces it
favorite  — preferred when it appears, ranked above unknown sites
normal    — met through search, no standing opinion
blocked   — never fetched, never stored (a written prohibition, or our own decision)
acquisition — how content from this site may legally reach our corpus:
fetch          — automated fetch is acceptable; no prohibition found
licensed       — we hold a licence or API agreement; terms recorded in `licence`
link-only      — store our own facts and link out; store no expression from the page
pending-review — starred but not yet legally reviewed; treated as `none` until it is
Notes below record what was read on the sites themselves on 2026-09-20.
They are a research summary, not legal advice.

allrecipes.com.note: People Inc. robots.txt prohibits scraping except to direct traffic, and names TDM, LLM/RAG use and dataset creation as prohibited. Licensing contact: contentlicensing@people.inc Licensable via People Inc Content Licensing.

americastestkitchen.com.note: Owner-starred 2026-09-20; reviewed same day, set to none pending a decision. Metered paywall, not a hard one: ingredients and numbered instructions are served to an anonymous fetcher within the meter, so the barrier is contractual and rate-based, not cryptographic. robots.txt carries NO legal comment block and does not disallow /recipes for generic crawlers, but does Disallow: / for anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, GPTBot, CCBot, PerplexityBot and others. Terms of Use (19 Aug 2026) contain NO scraping, AI-training, competing-product or republication clause - only the section 9 catch-all, 'Use of any of the materials for any purpose not expressly permitted in these Terms of Use is prohibited', over a licence limited to 'content and materials for which you have subscribed and paid for'. Quieter terms are not consent: a narrow grant plus paid access turns this from a copyright question into a contract one. No content-licensing or developer programme exists; majority owner is Marquee Brands (Feb 2023), a brand licensor. Only published contact: cooks@americastestkitchen.com. No recipe-copying litigation found, but that is weak evidence - Lumen's takedown corpus is CAPTCHA-gated and was not queried.

seriouseats.com.note: Owner-starred 2026-09-20; reviewed same day. A People Inc brand since September 2020 (People Inc = Dotdash Meredith, renamed July 2025), governed by the People Inc Terms of Service. Scraping is prohibited by CONTRACT, not by robots.txt: `User-agent: *` disallows only /embed? and /cdn-cgi/, so recipe URLs are not robots-disallowed for a generic crawler. But ToS 3.3(e) bars spiders, scrapers and crawlers (public search engines excepted, 'but not caches or archives'); 3.3(f) bars using the data to train ML or AI; 3.3(g) bars accessing the Services 'to build a similar or competitive website, application, or service'; 3.3(h) bars republication; 3.3(m) says any unauthorised use immediately terminates the licence. New York law, SDNY forum. ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai and FirecrawlAgent all get Disallow: / . IMPORTANT: these recipes are commercially LICENSABLE from the same company. People Inc Content Licensing advertises a recipe API with 'complete data, including method and images', 'Caching Permitted', and broad multi-channel usage rights. Pricing not published. Licensing is the intended route here, not scraping: contentlicensing@people.inc (permissions: CLPermissions@people.inc).

simplyrecipes.com.note: Identical People Inc. language to allrecipes.com. Licensable via People Inc Content Licensing.
